title: Check whether a sentence uses every letter
summary: A text editor can label a sentence as a pangram when it contains every English letter. Ignore case and non-letter characters when checking coverage. Check whether a sentence contains every letter A through Z.
requirements: Ignore case, punctuation, spaces, and digits.
Return true only when all 26 English letters occur.
hints: Extract letters using a case-insensitive pattern.
Count distinct letters using a Set.

examples.label: Typical case
input: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

tests.name: Common case — ["The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"]
input: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

tests.name: Additional variation — ["Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow!"]
input: Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow!
